Hi Maria — copying the technical answers below. I also attached our runbook, a control-patterns doc, the KMS checklist, and a signed geolock attestation PDF for immediate review.

Q1 — Residency/Geolock\- Data residency: In Redwood Private (VPC) mode the customer configures a storage endpoint (S3 bucket or self-managed object store) inside their VPC. All model inputs/outputs and long‑lived artifacts are persisted to that customer-owned storage.
\- No automatic cross-region replication: We do not automatically replicate customer storage objects to other regions. Any cross-region replication must be configured by the customer or by an explicit integration workflow that you approve.
\- Control plane metadata: The Redwood control plane stores minimal metadata required for routing (tenant id, model version pointer, metric aggregates). This metadata does not contain customer text payloads. We can provide a dump of the metadata schema and a sample (sanitized).

Q2 — Deletion / Tenant erasure process\- How to trigger: Tenant erasure can be initiated via the Redwood Admin API (DELETE /v1/tenants/{tenant_id}/erase) or from the Console (Admin > Tenants > Erase). We also support signed, time-bound erase requests via our support flow for compliance cases.
\- Steps that run: 1) job schedules to delete objects from the customer storage endpoint (if storage is inside customer VPC, the delete is executed via the storage credentials you provide); 2) invalidate and zero out KV caches associated with the tenant; 3) purge control plane metadata and delete related tracing/metrics within retention window; 4) sweep backups and snapshots.
\- Backups and retention: By default, automatic backups (where enabled) are retained for up to 30 days unless you opt to shorten that retention at provisioning time. For compliance customers we can configure immediate snapshot deletion and shorter backup horizons as a contractual setting.
\- SLA / expected timeline: For VPC-hosted storage where deletes are executed against customer-managed buckets, the primary deletion completes within 72 hours in >95% of runs (depends on object count). Full certification (including backup sweep and control-plane metadata purge) can take up to 7 days depending on snapshot cycles. We will provide a deletion certificate once the job completes.
\- Audit logs: We emit auditable events for erase initiation, storage delete confirmations, and control-plane metadata purges. We can provide a sanitized audit log sample (redacted tenant identifiers) for review.

Q3 — KMS / keys\- Customer-managed KMS: Redwood supports BYOK via AWS KMS and external HSMs for encryption-at-rest. You can provide your KMS keys; Redwood never has access to key material for customer-managed keys.\- Metadata encryption: Control plane metadata is encrypted at rest; if you require envelope encryption with your keys we can arrange that in the Private deployment contract.

Attachments (for your review):
- vpc-data-control-patterns.pdf (PDF) — diagram of data flow and storage ownership.
- tenant-erasures-runbook.txt (TXT) — step-by-step deletion runbook and checklist.
- kms-integration-checklist.xlsx (XLSX) — steps to configure BYOK with typical cloud providers.
- geo-lock-attestation-signature.pdf (PDF) — signed attestation stating no automatic cross-region replication.

Notes on evidence and canary\- Canary run: We recommend a canary deletion against a non-prod tenant; ops will generate a sanitized audit sample and a deletion certificate.
\- Signed attestation: We can supply a DocuSign-wrapped attestation template (Neha has started a draft).
